name: AM-GM inequality
conditions: Variables are nonnegative; standard multiplicative form requires positive variables.
statement: For positive x_1,...,x_n, (x_1+...+x_n)/n >= (x_1...x_n)^(1/n), with equality iff all variables are equal.
strategy: Normalize if useful, group positive terms, then apply AM-GM with weights matching target exponents.

name: Cauchy-Schwarz inequality
conditions: Real sequences; denominators in Engel form must be positive.
statement: (sum a_i b_i)^2 <= (sum a_i^2)(sum b_i^2). Engel form: sum x_i^2/y_i >= (sum x_i)^2/(sum y_i) for y_i>0.
common_errors: Using Engel form with nonpositive denominator
strategy: Choose vectors or rewrite fractions so the denominator sum becomes controllable.

name: Hölder inequality
conditions: Usual real nonnegative form for olympiad use.
statement: A common form is (sum a_i^3)(sum b_i^3)(sum c_i^3) >= (sum a_i b_i c_i)^3.
common_errors: Applying without checking nonnegativity in the chosen form
strategy: Match factors so the target expression becomes the mixed product in Hölder.

name: Jensen inequality
conditions: Function convex on an interval containing all inputs; weights nonnegative and sum to 1.
statement: For convex f, f(sum w_i x_i) <= sum w_i f(x_i). Reverse for concave f.
strategy: Check the second derivative and domain before invoking Jensen.

name: Chebyshev sum inequality
conditions: Two similarly sorted real sequences.
statement: For similarly sorted sequences, average(a_i b_i) >= average(a_i) average(b_i).
strategy: Sort or establish monotonic pairing explicitly.

name: Rearrangement inequality
conditions: Two real sequences sorted in the same/opposite order.
statement: The sum of pairwise products is maximal when similarly ordered and minimal when oppositely ordered.
strategy: Order both sequences, then compare the target pairing with extremal pairings.

name: Vieta formulas
conditions: Polynomial roots counted with multiplicity.
statement: For a monic polynomial x^n + a_{n-1}x^{n-1}+...+a_0, elementary symmetric sums of roots equal signed coefficients.
strategy: Translate root constraints into symmetric sums before solving.

name: Quadratic discriminant
conditions: Quadratic ax^2+bx+c with a != 0.
statement: Real roots exist iff Delta=b^2-4ac >= 0; repeated root iff Delta=0.
strategy: Convert existence into a discriminant constraint.

name: uvw reduction heuristic
conditions: Symmetric polynomial/rational inequality in three variables, typically homogeneous.
statement: Many symmetric 3-variable inequalities can be expressed in u=a+b+c, v^2=ab+bc+ca, w^3=abc; extremality often reduces to two equal variables.
common_errors: Treating the two-equal reduction as universally automatic without justification
strategy: First verify symmetry/homogeneity; express in elementary symmetric quantities and justify reduction.

name: Euclidean algorithm
conditions: Integers, not both zero.
statement: gcd(a,b)=gcd(b,a mod b); repeated division computes gcd.
strategy: Reduce large gcd expressions using gcd(a,b)=gcd(a,b-ka).

name: Bézout identity
conditions: Integers a,b, not both zero.
statement: There exist integers x,y with ax+by=gcd(a,b).
strategy: Use extended Euclid to construct coefficients.

name: Euclid's lemma
conditions: p prime.
statement: If prime p divides ab, then p divides a or p divides b.
common_errors: Replacing prime p with arbitrary composite divisor
strategy: Factor the expression and use primality at the critical step.

name: Fermat's little theorem
conditions: p prime; for multiplicative form gcd(a,p)=1.
statement: a^p ≡ a (mod p); if p does not divide a then a^(p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p).
common_errors: Using p-1 exponent when p divides a
strategy: Reduce exponents modulo p-1 only after checking coprimality.

name: Euler theorem
conditions: gcd(a,n)=1.
statement: a^phi(n) ≡ 1 (mod n).
strategy: Factor n, compute phi(n), and reduce exponent when coprime.

name: Chinese remainder theorem
conditions: Moduli pairwise coprime in the standard simple form.
statement: A compatible system x≡a_i mod n_i with pairwise coprime n_i has a unique solution modulo product n_i.
common_errors: Assuming uniqueness modulo product when moduli are not coprime
strategy: Solve congruences locally then reconstruct.

name: Lifting the Exponent (LTE)
conditions: Prime p divides x-y, p does not divide xy; formulas depend on p and parity.
statement: For odd prime p with p|x-y and p∤xy, v_p(x^n-y^n)=v_p(x-y)+v_p(n). Special variants apply to sums and p=2.
strategy: Before LTE, explicitly verify prime, divisibility, coprimality, and parity conditions.

name: Legendre formula
conditions: p prime, n positive integer.
statement: v_p(n!) = floor(n/p)+floor(n/p^2)+... .
strategy: Sum floors until p^k>n.

name: Wilson theorem
conditions: p>1 integer.
statement: p is prime iff (p-1)! ≡ -1 (mod p).
common_errors: Using as efficient primality test in computation
strategy: Pair modular inverses among nonzero residues.

name: Residue pigeonhole principle
conditions: Finite residue classes.
statement: Among sufficiently many integers, two share a residue modulo m; differences then are divisible by m.
strategy: Map objects to residues and count classes carefully.

name: Infinite descent
conditions: Assume a minimal positive counterexample and construct a smaller one.
statement: A positive-integer counterexample cannot exist if every counterexample yields a strictly smaller positive counterexample.
strategy: Define the minimal measure before constructing the descent.

name: Pigeonhole principle
conditions: N objects placed into k boxes.
statement: Some box contains at least ceil(N/k) objects.
strategy: The main work is designing boxes that make a collision useful.

name: Inclusion-exclusion principle
conditions: Finite sets/events.
statement: |A∪B|=|A|+|B|-|A∩B|, generalized by alternating sums over intersections.
strategy: Define bad-property sets explicitly and enumerate intersections.

name: Double counting
conditions: Finite set of incidences/pairs.
statement: Count the same finite set in two different ways to derive an identity or inequality.
common_errors: Counting different underlying sets on the two sides
strategy: Name the counted set before counting it two ways.

name: Extremal principle
conditions: Finite or well-ordered candidate set.
statement: Choose an object maximizing/minimizing a useful quantity and exploit extremality.
common_errors: Extremal object exists but chosen measure gives no leverage
strategy: Choose a measure linked directly to the contradiction or desired structure.

name: Invariant method
conditions: A repeated operation preserves a quantity/property.
statement: If an invariant differs between initial and target states, the target is unreachable.
common_errors: Claiming invariance without checking every legal move
strategy: Test parity, residue, coloring, weighted sums, and graph components.

name: Monovariant method
conditions: A quantity strictly moves in one direction and is bounded/well-founded.
statement: A strictly decreasing/increasing bounded measure proves termination or forbids cycles.
common_errors: Measure is not strictly monotone for every move
strategy: Find an integer-valued energy or lexicographic measure.

name: Ramsey principle
conditions: Finite complete graph/coloring setting.
statement: Sufficiently large structures contain a homogeneous substructure; e.g. every 2-coloring of edges of K6 has a monochromatic triangle.
common_errors: Using a Ramsey number without proof/allowed citation
strategy: Use degree pigeonhole followed by local case analysis for small Ramsey problems.

name: Hall marriage theorem
conditions: Finite bipartite graph.
statement: A matching covering every vertex of left part exists iff every subset S of left vertices has |N(S)|>=|S|.
strategy: Translate choices to a bipartite graph, then verify Hall condition for arbitrary subsets.

name: Triangle similarity
conditions: AA, SAS proportional, or SSS proportional criteria.
statement: Similar triangles have equal corresponding angles and proportional corresponding sides.
strategy: Write correspondence order explicitly before taking ratios.

name: Ceva theorem
conditions: Triangle ABC with D,E,F on opposite sides or extensions; directed form handles extensions.
statement: AD, BE, CF are concurrent iff (BD/DC)(CE/EA)(AF/FB)=1 in the standard positive interior case.
strategy: Choose a consistent cyclic orientation of the three ratios.

name: Menelaus theorem
conditions: Triangle and three points on sides/extensions; directed lengths recommended.
statement: D,E,F are collinear iff the product of three directed side ratios equals -1 (or 1 in unsigned convention with one external point).
strategy: Fix directed-segment convention before multiplying ratios.

name: Power of a point
conditions: Point P and circle; secants/tangents interpreted with directed lengths as needed.
statement: For secant PAB, power(P)=PA·PB; for tangent PT, power(P)=PT^2.
strategy: Identify one point with two secants/tangents and equate powers.

name: Radical axis theorem
conditions: Two nonconcentric circles.
statement: Points with equal powers to two circles lie on a line, the radical axis; three pairwise radical axes are concurrent unless parallel.
common_errors: Confusing radical axis with line of centers
strategy: Translate equal products into equal powers.

name: Inscribed angle theorem
conditions: Angles subtend arcs/chords in a circle.
statement: An inscribed angle equals half the measure of its intercepted arc; equal chords subtend equal angles.
strategy: Track which chord each angle subtends.

name: Ptolemy theorem
conditions: Cyclic quadrilateral ABCD.
statement: AC·BD = AB·CD + BC·AD.
strategy: First prove cyclicity, then identify diagonal and opposite-side products.

name: Law of sines
conditions: Nondegenerate triangle.
statement: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C = 2R.
strategy: Use when angle information is cleaner than side ratios.

name: Law of cosines
conditions: Nondegenerate triangle.
statement: c^2=a^2+b^2-2ab cos C.
strategy: Use to eliminate an angle or convert quadratic length relations.

name: Stewart theorem
conditions: Triangle ABC, point D on BC; denote BD=m, DC=n, BC=m+n, AD=d.
statement: b^2 m + c^2 n = (m+n)(d^2+mn), with b=CA and c=AB.
strategy: Draw labels explicitly before substitution.

name: Angle bisector theorem
conditions: AD bisects angle A in triangle ABC, D on BC.
statement: BD/DC = AB/AC.
strategy: Turn angle-bisector information into a side ratio early.

name: Spiral similarity
conditions: Two oriented segments or similar triangles with a common similarity center.
statement: A direct spiral similarity maps one segment to another via rotation+dilation; its center often lies at intersection of circumcircles/angle loci.
use_when: two segments with equal subtended angles
common_errors: Asserting a spiral center without proving angle/ratio correspondence
strategy: Search for equal oriented angles showing two triangles are directly similar.

name: Homogenization
conditions: Problem has a normalization or expressions of mixed degree.
statement: Introduce an appropriate scale/constraint so all terms have the same degree.
strategy: Identify scaling behavior and use a legitimate normalization.

name: Substitution
conditions: A constraint suggests parametrization.
statement: Replace variables by new variables that encode positivity, product, sum, or geometric structure.
common_errors: Substitution not surjective onto original feasible set
strategy: State why every admissible original configuration is represented.

name: Proof by contradiction
conditions: Negation of target yields exploitable structure.
statement: Assume the desired statement is false and derive a contradiction with a hypothesis or established fact.
common_errors: Deriving only an unlikely statement, not a logical contradiction
strategy: Write the exact negation, especially for quantified statements.

name: Mathematical induction
conditions: Statement indexed by natural numbers; base case and inductive implication available.
statement: Prove P(n0), then P(k)->P(k+1) to obtain P(n) for all n>=n0.
strategy: Consider strengthening the induction hypothesis if the step stalls.

name: Symmetry exploitation
conditions: Problem invariant under variable/object permutations.
statement: Symmetry can reduce cases, motivate equal-variable extremals, or suggest symmetric invariants.
common_errors: Assuming WLOG an ordering when the expression is not fully symmetric
strategy: Verify invariance before imposing WLOG order.
